chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Qulawayh al-Qummi, from Sa'd ibn Abdallah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus who said: I heard a man from the Tayyara narrating to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) from Yunus ibn Dhabyan that he said:

I was in one of the nights while performing Tawaf, when a call came from above my head: 'O Yunus, indeed I am Allah, there is no god except Me, so worship Me and establish the prayer for My remembrance.' I raised my head and behold, it was 'J' [Jibril]. Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) became furious, unable to control himself, and said to the man: 'Get away from me. May Allah curse you, and curse the one who narrated this to you, and curse Yunus ibn Dhabyan a thousand curses followed by another thousand curses, each curse sufficient to reach you to the bottom of Hell. I bear witness that no one called out to him except a Shaytan. Indeed, Yunus is with Abu al-Khattab in the severest of punishments, bound together, and their companions with that Shaytan, with Pharaoh and the family of Pharaoh, in the severest of punishments. I heard this from my father (peace be upon him).'

Yunus said: The man stood up from him, and he had not reached the door except for ten steps when he fell unconscious, vomited his bile, and was carried away dead. Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: An angel came to him with a column in his hand and struck him on his head with a blow that turned his bladder inside out so he vomited his bile, and Allah hastened his soul to the Hawiya and joined him with his companion who narrated to him, with Yunus ibn Dhabyan, and he saw the Shaytan who used to appear to him.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الرِّمَا: Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), the 8th Imam
key_terms.يُونُسُ بْنُ ظِبْيَانَ: Yunus ibn Dhabyan, a companion of the Imams

ai.seo_question: What happened to Yunus ibn Dhabyan when he heard the call during Tawaf?
ai.summary: This narrative from Rijal al-Kashshi highlights the Shia doctrine of *al-Ghuluw* (exaggeration in divinity), where Yunus ibn Dhabyan mistakenly attributed divine status to a Shaytan during Tawaf, confusing it with the Angel Jibril. Imam al-Rida’s severe curse and the immediate death of the narrator illustrate the gravity of this theological error, linking Yunus to Pharaoh as a precursor to the *Ghulat* sect. The incident serves as a critical case study in early Shia hadith criticism for distinguishing between true divine attributes and satanic mimicry.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/291] Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad b. Qulawayh al-Qummi from Sa’d b. Abdallah from Muhammad b. Isa from Yunus who said: I heard a man from the Tayyara recounting for Abi al-Hasan al-Ridha عليه السلام that Yunus b. Dhabyan had said:

I was making the Tawaf in one of the nights when I heard a call coming from above my head saying: ‘O Yunus - it is I who am Allah there is no god except Me - so worship Me and establish the prayer for my remembrance’ [20:14]. I raised my head to look up and lo and behold it was “J” (alluding to Jibril). Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام became furious at hearing this, a fury such that he could barely control himself and said to the man: Get away from me may Allah curse you, may He curse the one who reported this to you, and may He curse Yunus b. Dhabyan a thousand curses followed by another thousand curses, each curse sufficient to expel you to a pit of Hell. I bear witness that no one called out to him except a Shaytan. Verily Yunus is together with Abi al-Khattab in the severest of punishments, bound together with their followers unto that Shaytan, together with Firaun and the people of Firaun in the severest of punishments. I heard this from my father عليه السلام

Yunus [b. Abd al-Rahman] said: The man stood up to depart, he had not reached the door and made but ten steps when he fell unconscious, vomited out his excrement and was carried away dead. Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام said: An angel bearing a column came to him and struck him on the head such a blow that his bladder reversed [upside down] and he vomited excretion. Allah hastened his soul to the Hawiya and joined him with his fellow who informed him of this, with Yunus b. Dhabyan, and he saw the Shaytan who used to appear to him.
